entities.name: Adolphe Gesché
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adolphe Gesché (1928–2003) was a Belgian Catholic theologian and priest who became one of the most creative and widely read Catholic philosophical theologians of the late twentieth century. Born in Brussels, he was ordained a priest and spent his entire academic career at the Catholic University of Louvain, where he became professor of systematic theology.

Gesché's major work, the seven-volume series 'Dieu pour penser' (God for Thinking, 1993–2003), explored the relationship between Christian faith and the deepest questions of human existence—destiny, evil, the cosmos, human dignity, and eschatology. His theology was distinguished by its engagement with literature, poetry, and philosophy as interlocutors for theological reflection, and by its conviction that authentic Christian thought must emerge from genuine encounter with the human condition rather than from defensive apologetics.

His influence extended far beyond academic theology: his accessible, humanistic writing reached educated general readers in the French-speaking Catholic world and beyond. He was a regular contributor to public debate on religious questions in Belgium and wrote in Le Monde and other major publications. Gesché's theology, formed in the Belgian tradition of engagement with modern thought, represents one of the most significant contributions of twentieth-century European Catholic intellectual life.

entities.summary: Adolphe Gesché was a Belgian Catholic priest and theologian. He was professor of Dogmatic Theology at the Faculty of Theology of the Catholic University of Louvain and author of several works in the field of Theological studies.
